key_insight: GWDM combines wavelet-based diffusion with histopathology-specific guidance to generate realistic tissue image patches for training-data augmentation.
clinical_relevance: Synthetic patches improved nuclei and tissue segmentation in reported experiments, suggesting research value for data-limited workflows rather than established clinical benefit.
method: Use wavelets to capture image details at multiple scales.
Condition generation on tissue patterns and staining variations.
Gradually introduce histomorphological guidance, including perceptual and structural similarity losses, to stabilize training.
evidence_signal: Across BCSS, MoNuSeg, and PAIP2019, the abstract reports better synthesis than state-of-the-art comparators and improved segmentation with synthetic-data augmentation, but provides no numerical effect sizes.
watch_item: Generalization to unseen laboratories and staining protocols requires validation before clinical deployment.
paper_title: GWDM: A Guided Wavelet Diffusion Model for Realistic Histopathology Image Generation
